root_cause: SQLite's 'disallow unsafe SQL functions from untrasted schema content' protection was implemented by checking whether the current parse was a nested sub-parse of a top-level statement, or whether a specific expression was parsed directly from schema/DDL text. It did not account for virtual-table modules that, having been granted SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS status (and thus made usable from untrusted schemas), independently compile their own fresh top-level SQL statements built from schema-derived strings. Those internally-generated statements were indistinguishable, from the enforcement code's point of view, from ordinary trusted top-level user SQL, so the protection silently did not apply to them.
findings: Commit 4b136ed70a marks the FTS3 virtual table as SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS (ext/fts3/fts3.c, fts3DeclareVtab), lowering its eVtabRisk to zero so that FTS3/4 tables can be created and used even when PRAGMA trusted_schema=OFF (i.e. from untrusted/attacker-influenced schemas, such as those found in an attached or shared database).
